scope: Additional tightly bounded island systems with explicit food-area or land-pressure evidence

promotion_audit.decision: No record clears every promotion gate. Aneityum has an exact EU5 island tag and two independently similar population reconstructions, but its sources reconstruct contact-era population rather than a documented Malthusian equilibrium. Tikopia and Sikaiana have unusually explicit food-area pressure/carrying-capacity evidence but no EU5 location boundary.

records.label: Aneityum (Anatom), Vanuatu, eve of European contact
pressure_evidence: Spriggs applied a Bayliss-Smith energetic-input/output method to intensively surveyed cultivated land and obtained a broadly similar pre-contact range.
Independent epidemic back-calculation from documented nineteenth-century censuses gives approximately 4,800–6,100 people on the eve of contact, with a central estimate near 5,500.
Archaeological and ethnographic evidence documents intensive taro and other subsistence-garden systems; the island subsequently lost over 96% of its population after European contact.
records.boundary_description: Entire Aneityum island, southern Vanuatu; the EU5 location tag is island-specific.
records.boundary_source: Aneityum population reconstruction and Vanuatu island geography
records.notes: Strong exact-boundary validation case, not a scale anchor: the 4,800–6,100 interval is a contact-era population reconstruction and the independent methods do not establish what fraction of intrinsic 1337 capacity was occupied. Retain saturation fields null until pre-contact pressure evidence is separated from the reconstruction inputs.

records.label: Tikopia island subsistence system
pressure_evidence: Aerial-photo land accounting measured about 4.42 km2 total and 3.90 km2 cultivable, with 0.27 ha per person including fallow.
The 1929 population of 1,278 was judged near the maximum under the then-stable agricultural system; the 1,753 population in 1952 required an unsustainably short fallow and caused severe food stress.
The study documents local taro, breadfruit, bananas, coconuts, fish and wild fruits and explicitly models calorie/protein requirements.
records.boundary_description: Entire Tikopia island; no EU5 location or area tag is currently present.
records.boundary_source: Hervad-Jørgensen aerial-photo and food-area carrying-capacity study
records.notes: This is one of the clearest local-food pressure cases found, but it cannot be scored until Tikopia is represented by a verified EU5 island polygon. Its 1929/1952 dates are also far outside the 1337 target. Do not infer a saturation interval from the 1929 point without an independent pre-contact demographic series.

records.label: Sikaiana (Stewart Islands) atoll subsistence limit
pressure_evidence: Sikaiana archival synthesis reports a resident population stable around 200–250 despite a much larger diaspora, indicating a local resource limit.
Bayliss-Smith's ecological carrying-capacity estimate is explicitly 215–430 people for the atoll.
The atoll is small, with subsistence based on local gardens, coconut, fishing and communal food redistribution; the evidence is not a city or trade-hub estimate.
records.boundary_description: Entire Sikaiana atoll (Stewart Islands), Solomon Islands; no matching EU5 island tag is present.
records.boundary_source: Sikaiana Archives ethnography and Bayliss-Smith carrying-capacity estimate
records.notes: The carrying-capacity range is unusually explicit but is reported through a later ethnographic synthesis and cannot be promoted without an EU5 boundary and independent pre-1337 pressure evidence. The 1900–1930 resident population is also affected by migration, so this remains validation-only.
